page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is an x86_64 virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and includes 50 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core and text processing tests. However, multi-core performance is weaker, with Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained; while large-block read/write bandwidth is average, small-block cached read bandwidth is weak, and the PassMark memory score is in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that benefit from high single-thread burst performance but do not require sustained multi-core execution or heavy memory bandwidth. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention tradeoffs. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, static web serving, and small-scale development environments.
